newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian land dealer escapes PLO prison.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian land dealer escapes PLO prison.

text.p: A Palestinian land dealer said on Sunday at a news conference organised by Jewish settler leaders he had escaped from a PLO prison in the West Bank after being tortured.
Aharon Domb, head of the Council of Jewish Settlements in Judea and Samaria (the West Bank), said the fugitive he identified only as Mohammad sought refuge in Israel after his escape.

Wearing sunglasses, Mohammad said he was jailed after being summoned for interrogation by the Palestinian Preventive Security agency from his home in the village of Bidyah near the West Bank city of Nablus.
"They told me I would stay for a few hours but I remained in prison for two months," he told reporters.
Preventive Security officials identified the man as Ihsan Mohammad Salameh, 50, from Bidyah but said he was only a witness to sales of Palestinian land to Israelis, not a land dealer himself.
They confirmed he had escaped from prison in Nablus last week after they had finished interrogating him.
Salameh and his family, the officials said, were long-time holders of Israeli identification cards issued to Palestinians who cooperate with Israeli security authorities.
The Palestinian Authority had said it was holding around 20 Palestinian land dealers for interrogation.

In its battle against expansion of Jewish settlements on land Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East war, the Authority adopted a Jordanian military law which considers Arab land dealers traitors who could face life imprisonment or execution.
Three Palestinian land dealers have been killed in recent months in mysterious circumstances. Israel accused the Authority of the killings, but the PLO denied it was involved.

"They asked me to give them information on land sales and I did, then I spent two very difficult weeks. I was tortured. They would wip me with electric wires and tie my hands to the ceiling," Mohammad said.
"They made us work on construction of a building near the prison. I escaped during work hours and ran from Nablus to Bidyah. My family, who also have Israeli identities, took me to Israel," he said.

An Israeli participant at the news conference, settler lawyer Michael Teplow, called on the Israeli government to take "immediate action against the PLO to help us help land dealers, to give them refuge and recognise that they have helped Israel by selling land to Jews".
